answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
Let the inner radius be \(r\) m.
Inner circumference \(= 2\pi r = 440\)
\(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 440\)
\(r = \frac{440 \times 7}{44} = 70\) m
The track is 14 m wide, so outer radius \(= 70 + 14 = 84\) m.

So, the radius of the outer circle is 84 m.

answers.label: Q2
answers.solution:
Let the son's present age be \(x\) years. Then Shyam's present age is \(4x\) years.
Five years ago: son \(= x - 5\), Shyam \(= 4x - 5\).
\(4x - 5 = 9(x - 5)\)
\(4x - 5 = 9x - 45\)
\(5x = 40\), so \(x = 8\).
Shyam's age \(= 4 \times 8 = 32\) years.
Check: five years ago, Shyam was 27 and his son was 3, and \(27 = 9 \times 3\).

So, Shyam is 32 years old.

answers.label: Q4
answers.solution:
The printed expression carries a stray "?" after the small bracket; it is read here as a printing mark and ignored.
Work from the innermost bracket outwards, using the order of operations (division and multiplication from left to right, then addition and subtraction).
Small bracket: \(6 \div 3 \times 2 - 1 + 3 = 2 \times 2 - 1 + 3 = 4 - 1 + 3 = 6\)
Curly bracket: \(7 \text{ of } 2 - 6 = 14 - 6 = 8\)
Square bracket: \(5 - 2 + 8 = 11\)
Finally: \(16 - 11 = 5\)

So, the value is 5.

answers.label: Q6
answers.solution:
Ratio of ages \(= 2 : 4 : 8 = 1 : 2 : 4\)
Sum of the ratio terms \(= 1 + 2 + 4 = 7\)
First boy (2 years): \(\frac{1}{7} \times 70 = \text{Rs } 10\)
Second boy (4 years): \(\frac{2}{7} \times 70 = \text{Rs } 20\)
Third boy (8 years): \(\frac{4}{7} \times 70 = \text{Rs } 40\)
Check: \(10 + 20 + 40 = 70\).

So, the boys get Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 40.

answers.label: Q7
answers.solution:
Fewer students make the ration last longer, so this is inverse proportion.
Total ration \(= 180 \times 20 = 3600\) student-days.
Number of students for 25 days \(= \frac{3600}{25} = 144\)
Students who must leave \(= 180 - 144 = 36\)

So, 36 students should leave the camp.

45% of \(x = 270\)
\(\frac{45}{100} \times x = 270\)
\(x = \frac{270 \times 100}{45} = 600\)

answers.label: Q9
answers.solution:
Selling price of 3 apples = Rs 10, so selling price of 300 apples \(= \frac{10}{3} \times 300 = \text{Rs } 1000\)
Gain = Rs 400, so cost price of 300 apples \(= 1000 - 400 = \text{Rs } 600\)
Cost price of one apple \(= \frac{600}{300} = \text{Rs } 2\) (that is, 3 apples for Rs 6)
Gain % \(= \frac{400}{600} \times 100 = \frac{200}{3} = 66\frac{2}{3}\%\)

So, he bought the apples at Rs 2 each (3 for Rs 6) and his gain was \(66\frac{2}{3}\%\).

answers.label: Q10
answers.solution:
Required expression = given expression minus the result.
\((3x^3 - 5x^2 - x + 2) - (4x^3 + 3x - 5)\)
\(= 3x^3 - 5x^2 - x + 2 - 4x^3 - 3x + 5\)
\(= (3x^3 - 4x^3) - 5x^2 + (-x - 3x) + (2 + 5)\)
\(= -x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 7\)

So, \(-x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 7\) should be subtracted.

answers.label: Q12
answers.solution:
The comma between the two powers is read as a multiplication sign (the printed sign is lost).
\(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-5} \times \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\)
Using \(a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}\):
\(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\)
The bases are equal, so the powers are equal: \(8x = -16\)
\(x = -2\)

So, \(x = -2\).

answers.label: Q14
answers.solution:
The wording is unclear as printed ("13 m North West and 5 m South"). The numbers 13 and 5 point to a right-angled triangle in which his 13 m walk is the slanting side (hypotenuse) and his 5 m walk south is one side; the distance from the starting point is then the third side.
By Pythagoras' theorem:
Distance\(^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144\)
Distance \(= \sqrt{144} = 12\) m
(If the 13 m walk is taken exactly along the North-West direction at 45 degrees, the distance comes out as \(\sqrt{194 - 65\sqrt{2}} \approx 10.1\) m, which is not a value a calculator-free paper would set.)

So, he is 12 m from his initial position.

answers.label: Q15
answers.solution:
The figure is a quadrilateral with one side produced at each vertex, so 90°, 50°, 110° and x are its four exterior angles (one at each vertex).
The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is 360°.
\(90^\circ + 50^\circ + 110^\circ + x = 360^\circ\)
\(250^\circ + x = 360^\circ\)
\(x = 110^\circ\)
Check with interior angles: \(90^\circ, 130^\circ, 70^\circ\) and \(70^\circ\) add up to \(360^\circ\).

So, \(x = 110^\circ\).

answers.label: Q17
answers.solution:
Semicircle APC stands on AC and semicircle BPD on BD; each has radius 5 cm, so AC = BD = 10 cm, and the two semicircles touch at P, so AB = 5 + 5 = 10 cm. ABDC is a square of side 10 cm.
The shaded part lies in the top-left square of side 5 cm (from A to the middle of AB, down to P). From that small square, the arc AP cuts away a quarter circle of radius 5 cm (a quarter of semicircle APC's circle).
Area of the small square \(= 5 \times 5 = 25\) cm\(^2\)
Area of the quarter circle \(= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 5 \times 5 = \frac{550}{28} = \frac{275}{14}\) cm\(^2\)
Shaded area \(= 25 - \frac{275}{14} = \frac{350 - 275}{14} = \frac{75}{14} = 5\frac{5}{14}\) cm\(^2\)

So, the shaded area is \(\frac{75}{14}\) cm\(^2\), about 5.36 cm\(^2\).

answers.label: Q19
answers.solution:
Write the dividend in descending powers: \(-4x^2 + x + 6\).
Step 1: \(\frac{-4x^2}{x} = -4x\); \(-4x(x - 3) = -4x^2 + 12x\); subtract: \((-4x^2 + x) - (-4x^2 + 12x) = -11x\); bring down \(+6\): \(-11x + 6\).
Step 2: \(\frac{-11x}{x} = -11\); \(-11(x - 3) = -11x + 33\); subtract: \(6 - 33 = -27\).
Check: \((x - 3)(-4x - 11) - 27 = -4x^2 + x + 33 - 27 = -4x^2 + x + 6\).

So, the quotient is \(-4x - 11\) and the remainder is \(-27\).

answers.label: Q21
answers.solution:
Horse: SP = Rs 12000 at a loss of 20%.
CP of horse \(= \frac{100}{80} \times 12000 = \text{Rs } 15000\)
Cow: SP = Rs 12000 at a gain of 20%.
CP of cow \(= \frac{100}{120} \times 12000 = \text{Rs } 10000\)
Total CP \(= 15000 + 10000 = \text{Rs } 25000\)
Total SP \(= 12000 + 12000 = \text{Rs } 24000\)
Since SP is less than CP, there is a loss.
Loss \(= 25000 - 24000 = \text{Rs } 1000\)
Loss % \(= \frac{1000}{25000} \times 100 = 4\%\)

So, overall he has a loss of Rs 1000, that is 4%.

answers.label: Q22
answers.finalAnswer: A Rs 300; B Rs 225; C Rs 75
answers.solution:
A's one day's work \(= \frac{1}{6}\), B's one day's work \(= \frac{1}{8}\).
The work is finished in 3 days.
Work done by A in 3 days \(= \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\)
Work done by B in 3 days \(= \frac{3}{8}\)
Work done by C \(= 1 - \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{8} = \frac{8 - 4 - 3}{8} = \frac{1}{8}\)
The money is shared in the ratio of work done: \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{3}{8} : \frac{1}{8} = 4 : 3 : 1\)
A's share \(= \frac{4}{8} \times 600 = \text{Rs } 300\)
B's share \(= \frac{3}{8} \times 600 = \text{Rs } 225\)
C's share \(= \frac{1}{8} \times 600 = \text{Rs } 75\)

So, A gets Rs 300, B gets Rs 225 and C gets Rs 75.

answers.label: Q23
answers.solution:
Let the ages six years ago be \(4k\) and \(3k\).
Present ages: A \(= 4k + 6\), B \(= 3k + 6\).
Nine years from now: A \(= 4k + 15\), B \(= 3k + 15\).
\(\frac{4k + 15}{3k + 15} = \frac{7}{6}\)
\(6(4k + 15) = 7(3k + 15)\)
\(24k + 90 = 21k + 105\)
\(3k = 15\), so \(k = 5\)
A \(= 4 \times 5 + 6 = 26\) years, B \(= 3 \times 5 + 6 = 21\) years.
Check: six years ago 20 and 15 (4 : 3); nine years from now 35 and 30 (7 : 6).

So, A is 26 years old and B is 21 years old.

answers.label: Q24
answers.solution:
(a) The sign between \(13 \times 5^n\) and \(2 \times 5^{n+1}\) is missing in the print; it is read as a minus sign.
\(\frac{5^{n+2} - 6 \times 5^{n+1}}{13 \times 5^n - 2 \times 5^{n+1}}\)
Take \(5^n\) common above and below:
Numerator \(= 5^n(5^2 - 6 \times 5) = 5^n(25 - 30) = -5 \times 5^n\)
Denominator \(= 5^n(13 - 2 \times 5) = 5^n(13 - 10) = 3 \times 5^n\)
Value \(= \frac{-5 \times 5^n}{3 \times 5^n} = -\frac{5}{3}\)
(With a plus sign the value would be \(-\frac{5}{23}\).)

(b) HCF by division:
\(1309 = 1 \times 1071 + 238\)
\(1071 = 4 \times 238 + 119\)
\(238 = 2 \times 119 + 0\)
HCF \(= 119\)
LCM \(= \frac{1071 \times 1309}{119} = 9 \times 1309 = 11781\)
(Prime factors: \(1071 = 3^2 \times 7 \times 17\), \(1309 = 7 \times 11 \times 17\).)

So, (a) \(-\frac{5}{3}\); (b) HCF = 119 and LCM = 11781.

answers.label: Q25
answers.solution:
(a) The man and the train move in opposite directions, so the relative speed is the sum.
Relative speed \(= 49 + 5 = 54\) km/hr \(= 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\) m/s
The train passes him in 12 seconds, so its length \(= 15 \times 12 = 180\) m.

(b) The other train comes from the opposite side, so relative speed \(= 49 + 41 = 90\) km/hr \(= 90 \times \frac{5}{18} = 25\) m/s
Distance to be covered = sum of the lengths \(= 180 + 160 = 340\) m
Time \(= \frac{340}{25} = 13.6\) seconds

So, (a) the train is 180 m long; (b) it takes 13.6 seconds to pass the other train.

answers.solution:
Pipe fills in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{6}\) of the tank.
With the leak, the tank fills in 7 hours, so in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{7}\) of the tank.
Part emptied by the leak in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7 - 6}{42} = \frac{1}{42}\)
So the leak alone empties the full tank in 42 hours.

So, the leak will empty the full tank in 42 hours.

Spinning 3 hours a day for 12 days, time for 1 kg \(= 3 \times 12 = 36\) hours.
Time for 10 kg \(= 36 \times 10 = 360\) hours.
At 4 hours a day, number of days \(= \frac{360}{4} = 90\)

So, she will take 90 days.

answers.label: Q28
answers.solution:
Outer volume \(= 10 \times 8 \times 7 = 560\) cm\(^3\)
The wood is 1 cm thick on every side, so each inner dimension is 2 cm less:
Inner dimensions \(= 8\) cm \(\times 6\) cm \(\times 5\) cm
Inner volume \(= 8 \times 6 \times 5 = 240\) cm\(^3\)
Volume of wood \(= 560 - 240 = 320\) cm\(^3\)
Cost of wood \(= 320 \times 2 = \text{Rs } 640\)

So, the wood for the box costs Rs 640.

answers.finalAnswer: Food 120°, Rent 120°, Clothing 60°, Education 30°, Litigation 15°, Others 15°
answers.solution:
"pie & diagram" in the print is read as a pie diagram.
Total expenditure \(= 400 + 400 + 200 + 100 + 50 + 50 = 1200\)
Central angle of a sector \(= \frac{\text{expenditure}}{1200} \times 360^\circ\)
Food: \(\frac{400}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)
Rent: \(\frac{400}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)
Clothing: \(\frac{200}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 60^\circ\)
Education: \(\frac{100}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 30^\circ\)
Litigation: \(\frac{50}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 15^\circ\)
Others: \(\frac{50}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 15^\circ\)
Check: \(120 + 120 + 60 + 30 + 15 + 15 = 360\).
To draw: draw a circle of any convenient radius, draw one radius, and with a protractor mark off the angles one after another from it. Label each sector with its item and angle.

So, the sectors are Food 120°, Rent 120°, Clothing 60°, Education 30°, Litigation 15° and Others 15°.

answers.label: Q30
answers.solution:
Let the interior angle be \(I\). Then the exterior angle is \(\frac{I}{3}\).
Interior angle + exterior angle \(= 180^\circ\)
\(I + \frac{I}{3} = 180^\circ\)
\(\frac{4I}{3} = 180^\circ\), so \(I = 135^\circ\)
Exterior angle \(= 180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ\)
Number of sides \(= \frac{360^\circ}{45^\circ} = 8\)

So, the polygon has 8 sides.
